notes: source.mutex.guard.v1 (card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS, wave 32; mapped by card CT-CTWIN-LANE, wave 35; emission and native evidence added by card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION, wave 36). CT46 asks that a known shared wrapper holding a non-Sync but Send payload be accepted ONLY through a verified mutex protocol. Two of those words have no referent in this language and the mapping says so rather than pretending otherwise. There is no `wrapper` type at all -- no Arc<Mutex<T>>; the payload `buf` and the generation `m` are two separate names bound in one scope -- and there is no `Send`/`Sync` trait. What the language has instead is the transferability judgment's own classification: `let buf = protected 4;` is TransferKind::ProtectedResource, which qcore_core::transfer documents verbatim as "CT46's payload", sendable because custody really moves over a derivable synchronization edge and not freely shareable because ShareProtocol::CheckedMutex is its ONE sharing discipline in both the read and the write direction. The mapping therefore rests on the judgment's classification, not on a trait, and that substitution is the boundary this row publishes. The `accept` half is the case: the declared crossing `thread scope c share buf under m { ... }` lowers to a real Spawn/Join pair whose child takes the generation itself, and every reach of the payload by either task names a guard. The `only` half is the four refusing controls, each a different way of reaching the payload without the protocol and each refused by a distinct rule. WHAT WAVE 36 ADDED, and its exact boundary. The backend now renders a non-nested fork/join trace: the child is a real C11 thread created with thrd_create, it performs its own mtx_lock and mtx_unlock on the generation, and the creator reclaims it with thrd_join. The emitted C is compiled under ASan/UBSan/LSan and run, and its standard output is compared byte for byte with interpret_mutex_program's observation of the same checked trace, so mutex_reference_execution, c_emission, native_execution and native_sanitized now read `executed` on this case's own artifact. DELIBERATELY STILL NOT CLAIMED: contention, a data race, or any evidence about the C memory model. The checked trace is a total order in which the child's events are contiguous between the spawn and the join, so the faithful rendering spawns the child and immediately joins it -- the creator performs no trace event while the child runs. A rendering that let the creator run ahead would realise an order the checker never saw. The discriminating power of this row is therefore the byte-for-byte observation comparison plus the memory sanitizers, not a race detector: TSan is not run anywhere in this repository and no TSan-shaped claim is made (MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION-NO-CONTENTION). The no_crossing control still attributes the rendering to the crossing clause, and the guard_local control pins the emission boundary that survives: a guard-local child is outside both rendered shapes and is still published without C. TSAN CITATION (wave-39 close, 2026-09-18, discharging CT46-NOTES-PREDATE-TSAN-ROW on the CT07 precedent of docs/reports/tsan-rows-2/scripts/cite_ct07.py; a citation, not a stage flip - no stage of this row moves): the sentence above saying TSan is run nowhere in this repository describes wave 36's state and is superseded. Since wave 37 (card TASK-ROUTE-TSAN) the crossing has a ThreadSanitizer row on a CT46-shaped twin (crates/qcore-core/tests/unit/mutex_c_emit.rs), and since wave 39 (card TSAN-ROWS-2) on THIS fixture's own lowering: compiler/tests/task_route_tsan.rs::ct46s_own_case_runs_clean_bound_and_the_forcing_header_finds_no_seam lowers the case through compile_files, dies unbound at the one 0x18 fault, runs clean bound under ThreadSanitizer with stdout byte-identical to interpret_mutex_program's observation, and shows the schedule-forcing header attaches to nothing on this backend (the mutex backend calls thrd_create bare: no worker released, no schedule line). The row is serial by construction and claims no contention - the recorded decision: merge 0150c904 records MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION-NO-CONTENTION as RETIRED on its own second arm, in its words 'a DECISION, recorded as such, that this route's native evidence stays serial by construction', taken by card TSAN-ROWS-2 in its section 6 and recorded at that merge as accepted.

checked_mutex_crossing.attributed_to: the declared crossing `thread scope c share buf under m { ... }` -- the capture mode that requests ShareProtocol::CheckedMutex for a `protected` payload (TransferMode::ShareUnderMutex)

controls.note: The attribution control. The same route, the same payload and the same generation with the crossing clause removed: the checker admits it, the C backend renders it, and interpret_mutex_program returns the observation pinned above -- one WITHOUT any spawn or join line. Set beside the case's own observation, which carries `spawn 0 1` and `join 0 1` around the child's whole critical section, this is what makes the case's thread boundary attributable to the crossing clause itself rather than to the mutex route, the protected payload or this fixture's shape. Before card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION (wave 36) this control carried the opposite duty: it was the one program of the pair that rendered at all.

The `only` half, first way: the crossing is declared exactly as the case declares it, and the child then reaches the payload with no guard. Refused by the UNEDITED core -- Q611 is CheckedMutexInvariantV1's own code, not this route's -- which is the point card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS makes about where the soundness lives: a footprint a live generation protects has no unguarded access at all. Declaring the crossing buys the right to reach the payload under the protocol and nothing else.

The `only` half, second way: the payload is shared into the child with no protocol named at all (`share buf` without `under m`). Refused by name at the form, so a crossing cannot be requested without naming the discipline that admits it.

The `only` half, third way: a protocol IS named, and it is a real verified mutex generation -- it just protects a different payload. Refused. This is what makes `verified mutex protocol` mean the generation that protects THIS payload rather than any mutex the program happens to hold, and it is the control that distinguishes this mapping from a vacuous one in which naming any lock would do.

The `only` half, fourth way: the generation itself is shared instead of the payload. Refused by the transferability judgment, whose message names the kind and states the route's rule -- the checked-mutex route shares only a `protected N` payload and only under the generation that protects it. This control is what shows the judgment is consulted on the payload's kind at all, so the admission of the case is a classification decision and not a syntactic one.

The boundary the backend still does NOT cross, which is what keeps this case's now-executed emission stages a measurement rather than a claim that every mutex trace renders. A guard-local child (`thread scope c under g`) is created and joined strictly inside a critical section its parent holds, so the creator is not simply blocked for the whole of the child's segment and the fork/join rendering does not apply. The module checks -- it is admitted by the same route as the case -- and is published with c_source: None, interpret_mutex_program refusing at event 2, the GuardLocalJoin. Reachable from source, so the surviving refusal is not vacuous.
